description.narrative:
ANDI FOUNDATION har ansökt till Sida om finansiering på 6,7 MSEK för genomförande av projektet “Business in development facility Hub” under perioden 1 juni 2016 till den 31 jan 2022. Projektet syftar till att förbättra den ekonomiska situationen för kvinnor och män som drabbats av konfliken eller i konfliktdrabbade områden genom att underlätta införandet av småskalig produktion i värdekedjan hos ankar företag, genom inkluderande och miljömässigt hållbara partnerskap mellan den offentliga och den privata sektorn.
Den totala projektbudgeten är på 9,4 MSEK varav Sverige avser att bidra med 39%.

This contribution is a program support to ANDI FOUNDATION that aims at improving sustainable economic situation of women and men that have been affected by the internal armed conflict facilitating the inclusion of their small-scale production in the value chain of anchor companies, through inclusive and environmentally sustainable public-private partnerships. The starting point is to create feasible long term commercial relations through the coordination of different public and private allies that help to reduce gaps between the supply from small scale producers and the demand of anchor companies.
This is second phase of Sida’s contribution 52060045.

This contribution aims at improving sustainable economic situation of women and men that have been affected by the internal armed conflict facilitating the inclusion of their small scale production in the value chain of anchor companies, through inclusive and environmentally sustainable public-private partnerships.
Output 1: Small scale producers are strengthened and highly competitive and are engaged in inclusive and environmentally sustainable public-private partnerships. Output 2: Business sector includes competitive raw materials from small scale producers, as suppliers in their value chain. Output 3: The Hub is recognized by all stakeholders as an articulator platform that is able to facilitate inclusive business with real impact on improving the quality of life of the vulnerable population and with strong gender and environmental perspectives.

As mentioned before, by the end of 2019 an amendment to the agreement was signed with the aim of continuing to increase the number of partnerships, anchor companies, small-scale associations, partners and, consequently, direct beneficiaries. Despite the problems caused by the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the goals have almost been achieved. During the last seven years up to May 2022, the Andi Foundation has developed a total of 108 partnerships that contributed to improve sustainable economic conditions for 8,932 people (4,556 men and 4,376 women) in 23 Colombian regions, surpassing the 8,500 expected participants. This has resulted in the participation of 73 anchor companies in alliance with 2,240 small peasant farmer associations and 150 partners.
Between 2017 and 2022, 48 projects were terminated for various reasons such as: a lack of financial feasibility; the conditions were not viable for suppliers; lack of interest by companies or suppliers to continue with inclusive business models. 31 were successfully completed with stable commercial relations and good results indicators. The other 29 were in different stages up to May 2022: 3 were in the pre-feasibility phase; 5 were in the feasibility phase; 3 in enlistment; 11 were being implemented; 5 were in the completion phase with successful commercial relations.
Previous narrative reports contained progress indicators for 27 projects where families from the peasant farmer associations have, on average, increased incomes by 33%, and the associations have, on average, increased productivity by 9%. Other positive changes have been an increase in the ability for peasant farmers to regularly put money aside for their future wellbeing when they might be too old to be working and earning money. The anchor companies have also benefited from an average reduction in costs of 6.3%, by buying directly from peasant farmer associations thereby eliminating intermediaries. The alliance with organizations such as the Colombian Agricultural Research Corporation (Agrosavia is its acronym in Spanish) and Agrosavia has helped to bring technological advice to peasant farmers using virtual training methods on good agricultural and milking practices and climate alerts.
The Embassy's assessment is that the Andi foundation has achieved the expected results, in terms of the number of anchor companies, small peasant farmer associations and beneficiaries. The Andi Foundation has also adapted well in difficult circumstances when faced with the consequences of the COVID 19 pandemic.
The Embassy's assessment is that this contribution has been very relevant for improving sustainable economic conditions for women and men in conflict affected regions as it ensures sustainable commercial links with anchor companies. The Andi Foundation has complied with the planned objectives, the narrative report contains detailed information that fully corresponds with the logical framework and progress indicators. The external evaluation has also confirmed the important results achieved during the first three years and the need to continue using the methodology for new inclusive businesses in rural and conflict affected regions.
As regards of sustainability, the Embassy can be proud that a cooperation project that began in 2013 with Swedish support, has now become a seed for the institutional vision of the Andi Foundation. This cooperation project opened the ideas for an inclusive business model that started with small peasant farmers as suppliers to anchor companies, but which has now been widened to inclusive employment and distribution, as well as the inclusion of victims, ex-combatants, and ethnical minorities. The methodologies of all the inclusive business models have been developed during the last years as part of this project and are now at the heart of the strategic vision of the Foundation.
In addition, the Andi Foundation has developed the IN movement with the aim of visibilizing and recognizing companies that have worked with one or more of these inclusive models. This is also linked with the Emprender Paz award, that recognizes the positive impact of the private sector in peacebuilding, as inclusive business models mainly links anchor companies with small peasant farmers in conflict affected regions. The Andi foundation will continue using these methodologies and will therefore continue building alliances for promoting inclusive businesses. All the 29 partnerships, still active in this project, have continued operating with Andi Foundations own resources during the recent months.
The Embassy's assessment is that the Andi Foundation is a strategic partner with whom it will be relevant to continue working with in the future. Fortunately, it does not depend on international cooperation funds, but it does have an important added value that is complementary to many of other Swedish contributions related to peace building, such as reincorporation processes, victims reparation, the implementation of the peace agreement (integral rural reform), among others. The Embassy will promote alliances with other partners to fill the gap of commercial links for small peasant farmers and/entrepreneurs in conflict affected regions.
